title: Are LLMs Prescient? A Continuous Evaluation using Daily News as the Oracle
source_version: PMLR volume 267 published original; retrieved exact supplied PDF URL
summary: Date-related accuracy differences are supported descriptively, but the core inference identifying outdated representations and necessity of continuous pre-training is not established; released gold truncation, temporal summaries and chronology validation add material limitations.
limitations: No author code, model/API, generation or training was executed. Independent checks are synthetic logic/arithmetic examples, not raw-data replication.
Full QA/news datasets, response records, scoring/plotting code and historical prompts/configs unavailable within acquired source-only packet.
Separate OpenReview attachments unavailable behind 403/challenge. Bibliography not independently audited.
NASA current resource dates a path map to April 2023; exact historical 15-state count and original article first publication not independently recovered.

problems.location: Abstract; Sections4.2-4.3 pp.7-8; Fig5; eval.py127-128,183-187; qa-generation/utils.py
problems.judgment: Core mechanistic/necessity inference is not identified by changing-item observational comparisons.
problems.evidence: Fixed conditional ability with changed mixture gives declining accuracy; release truncates gold to512words while full article generates questions, so answer-preserving context is not guaranteed.
problems.counterevidence: High gold scores establish many answerable items; refusal-excluded declines persist; authors acknowledge generator/selection limits. None isolates mechanism.
problems.assumptions: Mixture examples show logical nonidentification, not actual mixture estimates; release historical equivalence is unproved; answer-span failure prevalence unknown.
problems.core_dependency: Central abstract/discussion conclusion about outdated representations and need for continuous pretraining, not the existence of benchmark accuracy differences.
problems.repair: Freeze generator/evaluator, audit answer spans/full gold, match difficulty/items, compare continued-pretraining intervention with retrieval/adaptation controls, or weaken causal claim.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: The abstract and pp.7-8 Gold/Need for Continuous Pre-training paragraphs connect date-related performance loss to outdated representations and the need for continued pre-training, whereas both the question distribution and generation system change. Section 4.1 distinguishes pre-cutoff historical questions from future questions; footnote 6 discloses a GPT-3.5/GPT-4 to GPT-4o-mini/GPT-4o generator switch after September 2024. The released eval.py truncates gold text to 512 words, while generation utils accepts 800-10000-character articles and supplies full text. These lines establish release behavior, not historical equivalence to Figure 5.
independent_check.decisive_check: Fresh total-probability constructions with unchanged conditional performance give 0.82 to 0.58 closed-book accuracy as remembered-item fraction moves 0.8 to 0.2 (accuracies 0.9/0.5), and 0.90 to 0.75 gold accuracy as easy-item fraction changes identically (0.95/0.70). Independently constructed an admissible 5644-character, 513-word article whose only answer is word 513; the 512-word prefix loses it. The first construction disproves identification of representation deterioration from aggregate drift; the second disproves an automatic answer-preservation guarantee.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: Actually inspected Figure 5's high gold scores and p.18 Figure 11's decline after refusal exclusions: the problem is not that all questions are unanswerable or that refusals alone explain the trend. The generator switch cannot explain the entire earlier decline. Authors' p.9 limitations and category distributions are meaningful but do not identify matched difficulty or the causal mechanism. No estimate of actual mixture shift/truncation prevalence or historical released-code identity is asserted. Gold reading comprehension is also not itself future forecasting.
independent_check.result: Major retained for a central explanatory/necessity conclusion, while descriptive benchmark declines remain supported. Repair requires frozen generators and evaluators, answer-span/full-context checks, matched items/difficulty, and a continued-pretraining intervention compared with retrieval/adaptation; alternatively weaken the causal/necessity wording. Report status updated to reflect this acceptance and exact final TeX rebuilt.

problems.judgment: Expanding slope is not local acceleration; YoY averaging masks are insufficiently specified.
problems.evidence: Monthly lambda.995 has138.28monthhalf-life; a single step with constant post-level yields increasingly negative expanding slopes. Several All means lie outside Pre/Post convex hull under exhaustive partition interpretation.
problems.counterevidence: Expanding coefficients valid as descriptive summaries; omitted straddling intervals/different masks could explain table. No raw-data arithmetic error proved.
problems.repair: Disclose monthly values, denominators, mask/weight/alignment definitions; estimate separate level/slope changes and clustered uncertainty.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Section 4.3 describes a five-month moving average and expanding weighted linear regressions with lambda=0.995 after the initial ten months. These are accumulated coefficients, not local derivatives. The Table 3 convex-hull check assumes Pre/Post are an exhaustive disjoint partition of the same nonnegatively weighted observations used for All.
independent_check.decisive_check: Fresh standard-library WLS on accuracy 0.8 in months 1-36 and constant 0.6 thereafter, using a trailing five-month mean and dropping the first four incomplete means, gives slopes -0.0002252373, -0.0030777340, -0.0049540611, -0.0051969334 at end months 37,42,48,60. Post-change raw slope is zero. The monthly weight half-life is 138.282573 months and the 59-month-old relative weight is 0.743980862. Table 3 TF GPT-3.5 (-4.33,-3.43,-2.84) and MC Claude (-6.26,-11.78,-5.03) violate the convex-hull implication under the stated partition interpretation.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: The synthetic alignment is explicitly declared and is not a reconstruction of the authors' Figure 6. Expanding regression remains a valid descriptive statistic. Distinct masks, weights or omitted cutoff-straddling intervals can explain the table; no raw-data arithmetic error is established. Annual means cannot recover monthly YoY values. Headline relative reductions were independently recalculated at about 21.5523% and 11.3379%, preserving the published descriptive effect.
independent_check.result: Minor retained. Disclose monthly series, masks, denominators, weight/alignment conventions and uncertainty accounting for questions clustered within articles/events; distinguish level shifts from later slope changes. Evidence supports interpretive and reproducibility limits without negating the observed aggregate drop.

problems.judgment: Publication date and filtered-item agreement do not certify earliest answerability or full filter validity.
problems.evidence: Prompt example uses May28event for May29publication; eclipse path mapped in NASAresource datedApr2023. Nonanswerabilitykappa.02;51/60acceptanceconditionalWilson~.739-.919.
problems.counterevidence: Seven explicitcriteria and60item4rateraudit are meaningful; historical earliest disclosures and dataset-wide issue prevalence not measured.
problems.repair: Dated-primary-evidence audit of accepted/rejected items; distinguish scheduled/calculable facts from unresolved outcomes; stratify generator/time.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Section 3.1, Appendix A.3-A.4, Table 4 and the filtering prompts aim to select questions not answerable before publication. Figure 23 describes a May 28 heat event in a May 29 publication example, which establishes event/publication mismatch but not the earliest public disclosure. Table 2's 2024 eclipse example concerns a scheduled/calculable event. The four-annotator, 60-item audit is of accepted items; 85% agreement-based acceptance corresponds to 51/60.
independent_check.decisive_check: Fresh read of NASA's primary eclipse-map resource found displayed publication date April 12, 2023 and a map description including the 2024 eclipse path. This supports prior path information only, not exact historical 15-state wording or archived 2023 bytes. Independently recomputed the 51/60 Wilson 95% interval as [0.7388541093,0.9190255942] under independent-item/fixed-label assumptions. Source Table 4 reports nonanswerability kappa 0.02, criterion agreement 83.33%, and mean kappa 0.26; kappa is not an error rate.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: The seven criteria and explicit human audit are positive safeguards. The publication/event difference alone does not prove that an answer was previously public; the current NASA page is not an archived snapshot or a reconstruction of the original article's first publication. Accepted-item sampling cannot estimate rejection sensitivity/specificity. Neither the conditional Wilson interval nor kappa establishes dataset-wide forecast-validity prevalence.
independent_check.result: Minor retained with Needs Evidence boundaries preserved for historical earliest-answerability and prevalence. Repair is a dated-primary-evidence audit of both retained and rejected questions, separating scheduled/calculable facts from unresolved outcomes and stratifying generator/time periods; no blanket claim that the benchmark is contaminated is supported.

problems.judgment: Inclusive prose differs from strict date-bound implementation/formula; released model alias and unseeded paths limit exact reproducibility.
problems.repair: Specify timestamp/timezoneinclusive/exclusive rules, immutable endpoints/seeds/prompts, scoring/refusalparser and rawoutputs.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: The p.5 prose includes news up to the preceding day, while the printed half-open interval and rag.py lines 34-36/52-53 use strict less-than boundaries. Table 5 names gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, but released eval.py maps to an unversioned GPT-3.5 alias. Randomized generation/selection lines lack local seeds, although main.py explicitly sets random_state=42 for a separate path.
independent_check.decisive_check: Fresh date comparison for resolution January 10 includes January 8 but excludes January 9 under newsdate < yesterday. Static reading confirms retrieval NUM=10 but eval.py passes only its first five contexts, agreeing with the paper's five-context input. Checked model-map lines and random.shuffle/choice/randint call sites, retaining the seeded main.py path as counterevidence.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: The implementation matches the displayed half-open formula, so this is a prose/boundary specification inconsistency and loss of the preceding day's context, not a demonstrated future-information leak. Unversioned alias and locally unseeded calls are release reproducibility limits; historical experiment endpoints/configuration are not proved by current source alone. No author program was run.
independent_check.result: Minor retained. Specify time zones, timestamps and inclusive/exclusive rules, immutable endpoint versions, run dates, prompt/parser/scorer versions, seeds and raw outputs. The correct five-context behavior is expressly excluded from the defect claim; exact historical score impact remains Needs Evidence.
